question: What's a good solar generator with panels for home backup?
query: best solar generators for home backup 2026 EcoFlow Anker SOLIX BLUETTI battery capacity solar panels comparison

replays.text:
For a **serious home-backup setup**, I’d look at the **[EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3](https://poweroutage.us/generators/best-solar-portable-generators)**. It has a 4,096 Wh battery, 4,000 W output with 120/240 V support, and accepts up to 2,600 W of solar input. It’s expandable, too, which helps if you want more runtime later.

**Check the bundle carefully:** the generator and solar panels may be sold separately. Choose compatible panels sized for its solar input, and confirm whether the listing includes them. For powering hardwired home circuits, you’ll also need compatible transfer equipment installed by an electrician; plugging appliances directly into the unit is simpler for essentials.

If you need strong 240 V output—for example, for a well pump—the **[Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus](https://ecosolarkits.com/blogs/guides/best-solar-generators-for-home-backup)** is another good option: it offers 6,000 W output and up to 3,200 W solar input. Neither unit’s runtime is a fixed number of days; it depends on what you run and how much sun you get.

For **serious home backup**, I’d look at the **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 with compatible solar panels**. It has a 4,096 Wh battery, 4,000 W output with 120/240 V, and accepts up to 2,600 W of solar input—useful for powering essentials and recharging during a longer outage. It’s heavy and typically a premium purchase, so check whether the listing includes panels; the generator and panels may be sold separately. [Specs and review](https://poweroutage.us/generators/best-solar-portable-generators)

If you need more output for 240 V appliances, the **Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus** is another strong option: 6,000 W output, 120/240 V, and up to 3,200 W solar input. [Comparison and details](https://ecosolarkits.com/blogs/guides/best-solar-generators-for-home-backup)

One important caveat: either setup is best thought of as **backup for selected circuits or essentials**, unless you add enough battery capacity and have the proper transfer equipment installed. What are you hoping to keep running—just fridge, lights, and Wi‑Fi, or things like a well pump or central AC too?

A strong all-around choice is the **[EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3](https://poweroutage.us/generators/best-solar-portable-generators)**. It has a 4,096 Wh battery, 4,000 W output with 120/240 V support, and accepts up to 2,600 W of solar input—good capacity for keeping essentials running and recharging during a longer outage. It’s heavy (about 113.5 lb) and a premium option.

If you need more output for 240 V appliances such as a well pump, consider the **Anker SOLIX F3800**: it offers 6,000 W output and up to 2,400 W solar input, according to the same [comparison](https://poweroutage.us/generators/best-solar-portable-generators).

One thing to check before buying: the listed solar-input capacity doesn’t mean panels are included. Confirm the bundle includes compatible panels, and plan on a transfer switch or home panel installed by an electrician if you want to power household circuits. ([Home backup guide](https://ecosolarkits.com/blogs/guides/best-solar-generators-for-home-backup))
